question: Who sets the prices of phone calls, video visits and commissary items in prisons and jails, and can the facility or sheriff keep a commission?

groups: articles and services as he deems proper

gold_sections.why: State prisons (Department of Corrections): debit or prepaid phone systems at the lowest available rates, and the Department may not receive any commission from them.

State prisons: the Director may prescribe reasonable rules and the fee for video visitation and electronic messaging; lowest available rates; the facility may not prohibit in-person visitation or receive any commission for installation or operation.
State prison commissaries: the Director may establish them and chooses the goods; no commission ban, but profits go to education, recreation, reentry or other purposes benefiting inmates.

Local and regional jails: the sheriff or jail superintendent may set and collect a fee for phone, video visitation and messaging systems (no lowest-rate rule or cap), no fee for communication within the facility or its appurtenance, and net profits must be used for inmate-benefit programs.

Sheriff-operated jail commissaries: the sheriff may establish the store and chooses its goods and services, net profits from inmate accounts go to inmate-benefit programs, the sheriff is the purchasing agent, and commissary funds and the inmate telephone services account are public funds.

Regional jail commissaries: the superintendent may open them, choosing the goods, with the approval of the regional jail board or jail authority, and their net profits must be used within each facility for inmate-benefit programs.

Subdivision 20: retail sales tax does not apply to goods a sheriff sells at a correctional facility under 53.1-127.1 or to prepared food sold within the facility, the only Code provision bearing directly on the price charged at sheriff-run commissaries.

"Local correctional facility" covers any jail or jail farm run by one or a combination of political subdivisions, so 53.1-127.2 reaches regional jails; "Director" and "Department" mean the Department of Corrections.

nuggets.text: The Department of Corrections must offer debit or prepaid phone systems, in addition to any collect calling, for calls to numbers on an approved call list.
nuggets.quote: The Department shall offer debit or prepaid telephone systems, in addition to any existing collect calling systems

nuggets.text: State prison phone systems must be set up with the lowest available rates.
nuggets.quote: Such telephone systems shall be established with the lowest available rates.

nuggets.text: The Department of Corrections may not receive any commission from its prison phone systems.
nuggets.quote: The Department shall not receive any commission from such telephone systems.

nuggets.text: The Director of the Department of Corrections may prescribe reasonable rules for prison video visitation and electronic messaging systems, including the fee collected for them.
nuggets.quote: The Director is authorized to prescribe reasonable rules regarding electronic visitation systems or electronic messaging systems, including Voice-over-Internet Protocol technology and web-based communication systems, for communication between prisoners and third parties and collection of a fee for the system utilized.

nuggets.text: A state prison that uses video visitation or electronic messaging must use the lowest available rates.
nuggets.quote: Any state correctional facility that utilizes such systems shall establish such systems using the lowest available rates.

nuggets.text: A state prison using these systems may not prohibit in-person visits and may not receive any commission for installing or operating the system.
nuggets.quote: (i) shall not prohibit in-person visitation and (ii) shall not receive any commission for installation or operation of the system

nuggets.text: The Director of the Department of Corrections may establish and operate state prison commissaries and decide what they sell.
nuggets.quote: The Director is hereby authorized to provide for the establishment and operation of stores or commissaries in state correctional facilities to deal in such articles as he deems proper.

nuggets.text: State prison commissary profits must be used for education, recreation, reentry and transition services, or other purposes benefiting inmates that the Director prescribes; no statute bars a commissary commission, but the profits are restricted to these uses.
nuggets.quote: The profits from the operation of such stores shall be used for educational, recreational, pre-release and post-release reentry and transition services, or other purposes beneficial to the inmate population as may be prescribed by the Director.

nuggets.text: A sheriff or jail superintendent running a local jail that uses phone, video visitation or electronic messaging systems is authorized to set up and collect a fee for them.
nuggets.quote: Each sheriff or jail superintendent who operates a local correctional facility that utilizes a telephonic communication system, an electronic visitation system, or electronic messaging system, including Voice-over-Internet Protocol technology and web-based communication systems, for communication between prisoners and third parties is authorized to provide for the establishment and collection of a fee for the system utilized.

nuggets.text: No fee may be charged for communication between prisoners and third parties within the jail or an appurtenance the sheriff or jail superintendent operates or controls. (The statute gives no examples; it is read here as covering, for example, video visits from terminals at the jail.)
nuggets.quote: However, no fee shall be charged for communication between prisoners and third parties within any local correctional facility or appurtenance thereto operated or controlled by the sheriff or jail superintendent.

nuggets.text: The net profits from jail phone, video and messaging systems must be used within the facility for education, recreation, medical, behavioral health, substance abuse, reentry and rehabilitative services for inmates, and may pay the staff or contractors who mainly provide those programs.
nuggets.quote: The net profits from the operation of such systems shall be used within each facility respectively for educational, recreational, or medical purposes for the benefit of the inmates to include behavioral health, substance abuse, reentry, and rehabilitative services for the benefit of inmates and may be expended to pay for the training, salaries, and benefits of employees or contractors whose primary job is to provide such programs and services to the inmates.

nuggets.text: A sheriff who operates a jail may establish and run a commissary that sells whatever articles and services the sheriff deems proper.
nuggets.quote: Each sheriff who operates a correctional facility is authorized to provide for the establishment and operation of a store or commissary to deal in such articles and services as he deems proper.

nuggets.text: In a sheriff-operated jail, commissary net profits generated from inmates' accounts must be used within the facility for education, recreation, medical and similar inmate-benefit services.
nuggets.quote: The net profits from the operation of such store that are generated from the inmates' accounts shall be used within the facility for educational, recreational or medical purposes for the benefit of the inmates

nuggets.text: The sheriff is the purchasing agent for the commissary and for nonappropriated funds received from inmates.
nuggets.quote: The sheriff shall be the purchasing agent in all matters involving the commissary and nonappropriated funds received from inmates.

nuggets.text: A regional jail superintendent may open commissaries, and choose what they sell, only with the approval of the regional jail board or jail authority.
nuggets.quote: The superintendent of a regional jail or regional jail farm may, with the approval of the governing regional jail or jail farm board or jail authority, provide for the establishment and operation of stores or commissaries in regional jail or regional jail farm facilities to deal in such articles as he deems proper.

nuggets.text: Funds from a sheriff-run commissary and from the inmate telephone services account are public funds.
nuggets.quote: The funds from such operation of a store or commissary and from the inmate telephone services account shall be considered public funds.

nuggets.text: Regional jail commissary net profits must be used within each facility for education, recreation, medical, behavioral health, substance abuse, reentry and rehabilitative services for inmates, and may pay the staff or contractors who mainly provide those programs.
nuggets.quote: The net profits from the operation of such stores shall be used within each facility respectively for educational, recreational, or medical purposes for the benefit of the inmates to include behavioral health, substance abuse, reentry, and rehabilitative services for the benefit of inmates and may be expended to pay for the training, salaries, and benefits of employees or contractors whose primary job is to provide such programs and services to the inmates.

nuggets.text: Virginia retail sales tax does not apply to goods a sheriff sells at a correctional facility under the jail commissary statute, or to prepared food sold within the facility.
nuggets.quote: Tangible personal property sold by a sheriff at a correctional facility pursuant to § 53.1-127.1 and sales of prepared food within such correctional facility.

office.value: State prisons: the Director of the Department of Corrections may prescribe reasonable rules and the fee for video visitation and electronic messaging and may establish commissaries and choose their goods; the Department provides the debit or prepaid and collect phone systems
Sheriff-operated jails: the sheriff may set and collect fees for phone, video visitation and messaging systems, may establish the commissary and choose what it sells, and is its purchasing agent

Regional jails: the jail superintendent may set and collect fees for phone, video visitation and messaging systems, and may establish commissaries and choose their goods with the approval of the regional jail board or jail authority

yes_no.value: State prisons: no commission on phones (the Department) or on video visitation and messaging (the facility); the prison commissary has no statutory commission ban, but its profits must go to inmate-benefit purposes. Jails: no Virginia Code section bars a commission, but net profits from phone, video and messaging systems and from sheriff-run and regional jail commissaries must be spent inside the facility on inmate-benefit programs, and sheriff commissary funds and the inmate telephone services account are public funds; federal FCC rules separately address commission payments

answer: Virginia's code says who decides, not actual prices. In state prisons, the Department of Corrections must offer debit or prepaid phones alongside collect calls [N1] at the lowest available rates [N2], and may take no commission from them [N3]. The Director sets reasonable rules and fees for video visits and messaging [N4] at the lowest available rates [N5]; prisons may not use them to ban in-person visits or take a commission on them [N6]. The Director may set up prison commissaries and choose their goods [N7]; no statute bans a commissary commission, but profits must benefit prisoners [N8]. In local and regional jails, the sheriff or jail superintendent may set and collect phone, video and messaging fees, with no lowest-rate rule or cap [N9], but communication inside the jail or grounds it controls is free (likely including on-site video visits) [N10]. No Virginia Code section bars a jail commission, but net profits must fund inmate programs inside the jail, such as education, medical care and reentry [N11]. A sheriff may run a jail commissary and choose its goods [N12], must spend net profits from inmate accounts the same way [N13], and is its purchasing agent [N14]; commissary and inmate telephone funds are public funds [N16], and sheriff commissary sales are sales-tax exempt [N18]. Regional jail commissaries need board or authority approval [N15] and follow the same profit rule [N17]. Vendor contracts set actual rates; federal FCC rules cap audio and video call rates and address commissions (check the current order).

out_of_corpus.what: Caps on the rates and ancillary fees that providers may charge for interstate and intrastate audio and video calls from prisons and jails, and the FCC's treatment of site commissions paid to facilities (compliance dates and cap levels have been revised by later orders, so check the current one)
out_of_corpus.where: FCC inmate calling services rules, 47 CFR Part 64 Subpart FF, adopted under 47 U.S.C. 276 as amended by the Martha Wright-Reed Just and Reasonable Communications Act of 2022 (Pub. L. 117-338); FCC WC Docket Nos. 23-62 and 12-375

out_of_corpus.what: The actual per-minute call rates, video visit and message prices, deposit and account fees, any commission percentage paid to a jail, and commissary item prices and markups
out_of_corpus.where: The Department of Corrections' and each sheriff's or regional jail's contracts with phone, video visitation, tablet and commissary vendors (public procurement records under the Virginia Public Procurement Act and FOIA)

out_of_corpus.what: The Director's rules for inmate telephone service, video visitation and messaging fees, and commissary operations and pricing in state prisons
out_of_corpus.where: Virginia Department of Corrections operating procedures (vadoc.virginia.gov), issued under Va. Code 53.1-1.1, 53.1-35.1 and 53.1-27

out_of_corpus.what: Minimum standards for inmate telephone access, visitation and the handling and accounting of inmate funds and commissary in local and regional jails
out_of_corpus.where: State Board of Local and Regional Jails regulations (Virginia Administrative Code, Title 6, Agency 15, Minimum Standards for Jails and Lockups)

out_of_corpus.what: Each sheriff's or regional jail's fee schedule for phones, video visits and messaging, its commissary price list, and the detailed accounting specifications and actual audit reports for commissary and inmate telephone funds (the Code's basic duties, an official account for prisoner trust funds, books open to the Auditor of Public Accounts and inclusion in the local government audit, are in Va. Code 15.2-1615)
out_of_corpus.where: The sheriff's office or regional jail authority; the Auditor of Public Accounts' specifications for audits of constitutional officers and each locality's audit report

local_option: Each sheriff or jail superintendent decides whether and how much to charge for jail phone, video visitation and electronic messaging systems, with no statutory lowest-rate rule or cap, except that communication within the facility or its appurtenance is free (53.1-127.2); each sheriff decides what a sheriff-run jail commissary sells (53.1-127.1); a regional jail superintendent, with the regional jail board's or jail authority's approval, decides whether to open a commissary and what it sells (53.1-115.2). Commission percentages and prices are set in each jail's vendor contracts.
notes: Two regimes. State prisons (Department of Corrections): 53.1-1.1 (phones: debit or prepaid in addition to collect, lowest available rates, approved call list of no fewer than 20 numbers, no Department commission; the call-list size is left out of the nuggets because it does not bear on price or commission) and 53.1-35.1 (video visitation and electronic messaging: Director's reasonable rules and fee, lowest available rates, security needs; the facility may not prohibit in-person visitation or receive any commission for installation or operation; the Department may temporarily limit use in emergencies; 53.1-35.1 expressly excludes telephonic systems and court video systems). 53.1-27 state prison commissaries carry no commission ban but restrict profits to inmate-benefit purposes; the Corrections Private Services Act (53.1-261 lists commissary among correctional services) lets the Department contract commissary out. Local and regional jails: 53.1-127.2 authorizes the sheriff or jail superintendent to establish and collect a fee, sets no lowest-rate rule or cap (unlike 53.1-1.1 and 53.1-35.1), and bars a fee for communication 'within' the facility or its appurtenance; the statute gives no example, and it is read here as covering communication with a third party who is on site, such as lobby video visits. No Virginia Code section bars a jail from receiving a vendor commission; that is inferred from the absence of a ban and from the net-profit language of 53.1-127.2, 53.1-127.1 and 53.1-115.2, which assumes the facility receives revenue and directs it to inmate-benefit programs. Federal FCC rules under the Martha Wright-Reed Act separately cap audio and video call rates and address site-commission payments (the 2024 order barred providers from paying site commissions; its caps and compliance dates were later revised, so check the current order). 'Local correctional facility' in 53.1-1 includes facilities run by a combination of political subdivisions, so 53.1-127.2 reaches regional jails through their jail superintendents. 53.1-127.1 speaks only of sheriffs: the purchasing-agent rule and the public-funds status of commissary funds and the inmate telephone services account are stated for sheriff-operated jails, and the public-funds sentence names only commissary funds and the inmate telephone services account, not video visitation or messaging revenue. Regional jail commissaries are governed by 53.1-115.2 (board or authority approval; the same net-profit rule). The sales tax exemption in 58.1-609.1(20) covers sales by a sheriff under 53.1-127.1 and prepared food within the facility; it does not name regional jail superintendents' stores. 15.2-1615 requires the sheriff to deposit money received with the treasurer except for official accounts (including funds held in trust for prisoners, under State Board of Local and Regional Jails procedures), keeps the sheriff's books open to the Auditor of Public Accounts, and includes them in the local government audit; it is background to accounting for jail funds and is not a gold section. No statute fixes any dollar rate, commissary price or markup, and no statute found gives the State Corporation Commission authority over inmate call rates (56-508.15 only requires registration to resell intrastate service through pay telephone instruments). Juvenile correctional center stores (66-22.1) follow the same Director-run, profits-for-residents model but are outside this question. Jail standards in 53.1-68 require access to counsel by secure, confidential telephone or video conference that is not recorded or monitored, but say nothing about price.
